item.title: Izumo Taisha: Japan's Grand Shrine of En-musubi — Guide
item.description: Izumo Taisha is among the oldest and most important Shinto shrines in Japan, dedicated to Okuninushi, the deity of nation-building and, above all, of en-musubi — the forging of good relationships, in love and beyond. It is so revered that October, elsewhere called Kannazuki (‘the month without gods’), is known here as Kamiarizuki, ‘the month with gods’, because all Japan’s deities are believed to gather at Izumo. The shrine is famous for its colossal shimenawa straw ropes, some weighing several tonnes, and for a rare custom: worshippers clap four times rather than the usual two.
